inputs.source: Authenticated SSO chat question from the employee
Published HR policy documents, authored by the HR content team, two-person reviewed before publish

instructions.note: The 'do not give legal advice' rule relies solely on model compliance. Severity is low because no further sink exists beyond the chat reply, so the worst case is a misleading answer, not data loss or system compromise.

controls.name: Read-only credential scoped to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: The credential is read-only and scoped solely to the policy index. The model cannot act beyond this scope regardless of its behavior, so this does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Two-person review required before publishing policy content
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced in the HR publishing workflow outside the agent and independent of model behavior. It narrows rather than fully severs the injection path, since colluding or compromised reviewers could still approve malicious content.

controls.name: Network egress denied at the network layer, verified by pen test
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced and verified at the network boundary, independent of model behavior. It is scoped to the current component set; a new tool or MCP server provisioned with its own network path would not automatically be covered.

controls.name: Chat reply destination bound to the authenticated requester's own session
controls.decay_rationale: The reply destination is fixed by the authenticated chat session established before the agent acts, not chosen by model output. The model cannot redirect a reply to another party, so this does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Closes the classic covert channel where model output embeds a URL or image reference with encoded data that gets auto-fetched. Enforced by the client, independent of model behavior.

controls.name: Model is pinned; an upgrade requires a change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: Prevents a silent model upgrade from invalidating this assessment's assumptions without triggering a review. It does not itself reduce attack surface; it ensures reassessment occurs (ISO 42001 8.2).

controls.name: Prompt instruction: do not give legal advice
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to follow the instruction. A more capable or adversarially prompted model could rationalize legal-advice-like answers. Consequence is low given no further sink beyond the chat reply.

findings.title: Internal policy content reaches the authenticated employee via chat reply (intended function, residual exfiltration surface)

attack_path.note: Published, internally reviewed HR policy content
Reply (egress of internal data) sent to the authenticated requester

forecast.watch_signal: New entries in the tool manifest or an MCP client config, or any network/firewall policy change broadening what the agent or its environment can reach, particularly any outbound internet-capable tool or server not covered by the existing pen-tested egress block.

evidence.observation: The agent's credential is read only and scoped to the policy index (least privilege).
Replies go only to the authenticated requester's chat session; the chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links.
The agent has no other tools, no memory, and no network egress; egress is denied at the network layer and verified by a pen test.

recommendations.action: Maintain an explicit, version-controlled tool/MCP allowlist and require this assessment to be re-run before any new tool or MCP server with network reach is added.
Add an audit log of agent replies, including the policy snippets quoted, for compliance monitoring and post-hoc review.

findings.title: Indirect injection via HR policy content could bias agent replies, with a bounded blast radius

attack_path.note: Internally authored, reviewed policy text treated as trusted context
Model quotes or paraphrases policy text in its reply to the employee

forecast.watch_signal: The policy index begins ingesting content from sources other than the reviewed HR publishing workflow (for example, direct employee submissions or external feeds), or the two-person review requirement is relaxed to a single reviewer.

evidence.observation: The agent is instructed to use policy_search to find the relevant policy and quote it, which constrains output largely to source text rather than free generation.
Only the HR content team can write to the policy index, and publishing requires two-person review, narrowing the chance of malicious content entering the index.
No image rendering or auto link-fetching limits the payoff of any injected content, since no covert channel exists.

recommendations.action: Spotlight or delimit retrieved policy text distinctly from system instructions in the model context so the model cannot confuse quoted content with directives.
Periodically sample agent replies against the published policy text to catch drift or injected content that passed review.

rating.rationale: Both present-day findings are inherently moderate because internal-trust content reaches an egress-class (S2) sink. Residual drops to low because of layered, independent structural controls: a read-only scoped credential, two-person review before publishing, a reply destination bound to the authenticated requester's own session, a chat client that does not render images or auto-fetch links, and a pen-tested network egress block. No untrusted (U) source exists anywhere in this design, which is unusual and materially limits inherent risk compared to typical HR or ticketing agents that ingest external email or web content. The forecast rises to high because the controls holding residual risk down are narrow in scope: adding a new tool or MCP server with its own network reach, or relaxing the two-person publish review, would reopen an exfiltration or poisoning path that nothing else in the current design covers.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts (prompt.md, tools.json, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.
No MCP configuration or IaC was provided; the single declared tool and the absence of other tools, memory, and network egress are taken as declared rather than independently discovered.
The two-person publish review process and the destination-binding behavior are declared, not independently verified; only the network egress block is stated as pen-test verified.

max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes were not specified. The rubric's autonomy modifier was not applied because the design's single-turn, single-tool interaction pattern appears inherently bounded, but this assumption should be confirmed with the team.
